Replay

Angular correction smoothing

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Use Smoother2 and Smoother3 to ease displayed poses toward same-tick corrections. They retain rotational correction error as local presentation state, alongside positional error. Read complete detached poses:

Odin
// before and after belong to the same simulation tick.
view.smooth_correct_pose(&smoother2, before2, after2)
view.smooth3_correct_pose(&smoother3, before3, after3)

// The current pose includes ordinary movement/rotation; only correction error decays.
shown2 := view.smooth_present(&smoother2, current2, render_dt)
shown3 := view.smooth3_present(&smoother3, current3, render_dt)

The correction calls return false on invalid inputs without changing the smoother. Initialize by presenting a valid pose before applying corrections. 2D uses radians and the shortest signed angular difference. 3D uses x/y/z/w quaternions, normalizes valid nonzero values and treats q and −q as equivalent. It composes correction rotations in order; Euler-component subtraction is not used. The error angle decays exponentially with the same half-life as position, so splitting a render interval preserves the result within floating-point error.

Default correction cuts are 60 position units in 2D, 2.25 in 3D and π/2 radians for angle. A discontinuity, disabled cut, or correction exceeding either bound clears the complete pose error. Existing position-only correction calls remain available and clear angular error on their explicit/large cuts too. smooth_rebase additionally preserves the displayed 2D angle when rebasing a whole displayed pose; its existing position cut remains 48.

A finite nonpositive half-life disables smoothing. An invalid current pose, render duration or nonfinite half-life holds the previous shown pose and leaves state unchanged. Correction poses/cut parameters must be finite; 3D rotations must be nonzero. At the exactly-180-degree ambiguity a canonical quaternion sign chooses a stable error axis, so equivalent signs follow the same visual path. Simulation values and their checksums are never changed by these functions.

The Godot Body2 and Body3 adapters use these corrections and preserve the skin's authored local offset and rotation. Their physics publication still reads PhysicsServer. Their skin correction reads the node transform because a frozen kinematic solver can retain its previous transform until the next physics step after a node is placed. Reading that stale solver transform for rendering would accumulate a correction twice or apply the skin relative to the wrong parent transform.

Tests and evidence include native/default and optimized WASM corpus execution, a real Godot native and browser fixture, ownership transfers and both Slopball network games. These checks do not establish perceptual quality on every device or support arbitrary scaled/sheared hierarchies, contacts or deterministic Godot solver rollback.
